- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; reduce forecast dip depth or delay correction to allow for mean reversion.  
- If model consistently forecasts lower prices than true outcome over 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, increase baseline forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for lagged momentum.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.28, -0.67), model tends to underestimate recovery; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for rebound phase.  
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., 3–5% below), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 0.5–1.0% to reflect underlying trend persistence.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment volatility; if sentiment swings sharply, anchor forecast to 30-day moving average rather than 18-day trend.
